hero.title: Check-ups and cleans
hero.lead: New patients of every age are welcome. For a first visit we recommend a thorough consultation and clean, so your dentist can see the whole picture and find small problems before they become big ones.

intro.heading: Why regular check-ups matter
intro.html:
Tooth decay and gum disease often develop without pain. By the time a tooth aches, the problem is usually larger and treatment more involved. A check-up gives your dentist the chance to spot early changes and deal with them simply.

A professional scale and clean removes calculus (hardened plaque) that a toothbrush can’t shift. Left in place, it irritates the gums and makes gum disease more likely.
intro.aside_heading: Book a check-up sooner if you notice
aside: Gums that bleed when you brush or floss
Sensitivity to hot, cold or sweet food
A chipped tooth or a filling that feels rough
Persistent bad breath or a bad taste
A sore spot in your mouth that hasn’t healed after two weeks

callout.title: Prevention costs less, and hurts less, than repair.
callout.html: Regular check-ups let your dentist find decay, gum disease and wear early, when treatment is simpler. Ask your dentist how often you should come in; it depends on your own teeth and history.

process.heading: What happens at your visit
process.intro: We take sufficient time at each visit. Not every step is needed every time, and your dentist will explain what they’re doing and why.
steps: A careful look at every tooth, your gums and the soft tissues of your mouth.
Your dentist assesses how your jaw moves and whether there are signs of strain or grinding.
Close-up and full-face X-rays show what can’t be seen by eye, such as decay between teeth or below the gum line.
Intraoral photos let you see exactly what your dentist sees.
Plaque and hardened tartar are removed and teeth are polished smooth.
Applied to help strengthen tooth enamel.
If anything needs attention, you take home the most accurate estimate we can give of the time and cost involved.

care.heading: Before and after your appointment
items: Note any medicines you take and changes to your health, and any teeth that have been bothering you.
Tell your dentist if anything feels uncomfortable. They can pause or adjust what they’re doing.
Keep brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste and cleaning between your teeth. Your dentist will suggest when to come back.

faqs: Do I need X-rays every visit?
No. Your dentist decides when X-rays are useful, based on your history and what they see. They show decay between teeth and problems below the gum line that can’t be seen by eye.
Most people find a scale and clean comfortable. If your gums are inflamed or your teeth are sensitive, it can feel a little uncomfortable. Tell your dentist and they can go more gently.
Why do you give me a printed plan?
So you can see exactly what has been recommended and think it over in your own time. Nothing goes ahead until you’re ready.
cost: A check-up and clean is a standard appointment, but the final cost depends on what is needed on the day, such as X-rays.
